info.title: Ambivo Books & Accounting API
info.description:
Double-entry accounting engine, invoicing, bank reconciliation, and financial reporting.

## Authentication
All endpoints require a Bearer JWT token unless marked otherwise.
Obtain a token via `POST /api/v1/auth/login` (proxied to Core API).

## Multi-Tenancy & Entity Context
After login, call `POST /api/v1/auth/set-entity` to select the accounting entity (company).
Most endpoints require an active entity context stored in the server-side session.

## Single Entry Point
All requests go through `booksapi.ambivo.com`. Authentication, CRM entities
(customers, vendors, products, bills, payments), and other Core API operations
are proxied internally — clients never call the Core API directly.
## The list contract

Every register takes the same shape. Ship the whole filter, get one page and a
real count back in ONE request.

| param | meaning |
|---|---|
| `match_filter_dict` | JSON predicate tree, Mongo-shaped |
| `sort_dict` | JSON `{field: 1 \| -1}`; key order is significant |
| `page_num` / `page_size` | 1-based page number and size |
| `search_text` | free text over the fields that endpoint declares searchable |
| `get_count` | `true` for a real total; `false` skips the count query |

`page` and `search` are accepted as **deprecated aliases** for `page_num` and
`search_text`. The contract name wins when both are sent.

**Unknown query params are rejected (422), not ignored.** This is the point of the
contract, not a detail: a param the server does not recognise used to be dropped,
and the endpoint answered HTTP 200 with the UNFILTERED set — a wrong answer that
looks like a right one. A filter the endpoint cannot honour is likewise a 400
naming the offending key, never a silent full-table read.

**Every filterable field is declared per endpoint**, with the storage encoding of
the field, not just its type. That matters because an operator can be validated
from the value alone but whether a value will MATCH cannot: money is a Decimal on
one half of this API and a JSON string on the other, native Postgres enums compare
by member name while the API serialises the label, and one `timestamp` filter type
covers two different wire encodings. A wrongly encoded value produces a valid query
that returns nothing and reads as "no such records".

**Sorting is declared, not assumed.** Each endpoint publishes which fields it can
sort on, and that declaration matches what the server will actually do — a field
offered as sortable will sort.

On the Books-native registers that means an index has to back it: an unindexed
sort is a full scan plus a sort on every page, on a register that grows without
bound, triggered by whichever column a user clicks. A field with no index is
simply not offered as sortable; asking anyway returns `SORT_FIELD_NOT_SORTABLE`,
and `SORT_FIELD_NOT_INDEXED` if it is declared but its index has gone. The remedy
for a missing sort is an index, not a wider rule.

Core-proxied registers are not gated this way — their indexes live in the
platform API, which owns its own planner.

**`total` may be null** when `get_count=false` — that means *not counted*, NOT
zero. `has_more` is exact either way.

Where a total IS returned it is a real count of the filtered set. The bills and
payments registers previously reported the size of the PAGE as the total (page
size 10 gave a total of 10, on a tenant with far more); those now issue an
explicit count. If a count cannot be produced the field is null rather than a
page-sized number — a null total is honest, a page-sized one is a lie.

## Picklists

Reference data is read through `/{entity}/picklist`, which has two modes:

- **Browse** — `search_text` / `page_num` / `page_size`, for a dropdown.
- **Resolve** — `ids=1,2,3`, for reference columns.

Resolve exists so rendering a column of references costs one request rather than
one per row. Ids that do not resolve are returned in `missing`; they are not a
404, so a single deleted reference cannot blank a grid.

## Response Pattern

Responses are documented **as the service emits them, at the top level**. There is no
`data` envelope anywhere in this API, and most endpoints return the model directly
with no `result` key.

1. **Books-native paginated** — `{items, total, page, page_size, pages, has_more}`.
   No `result`. `total` may be `null` (meaning *not counted*, not zero) when the caller
   passes `get_count=false`; use `has_more`, which is exact. The field is `pages`, not
   `total_pages`.
2. **Core-proxied list** — `{result: 1, items, pagination}`, where `result` is a plain
   field of the model and pagination keys are `page / page_size / total_items /
   total_pages`.
3. **Bare model** — the response model at the top level, no envelope. Most endpoints.
4. **Untyped Core passthrough** — Core's envelope spread at the top level,
   `{result: 1, ...payload}`. Marked as such on the operations concerned.

**Errors** use `ErrorResponse`: `{result: 2, error_code, error: {message}}`.

**Money is serialised as a JSON STRING**, not a number (Pydantic `Decimal`). Parse
with a decimal type; do not use a float.


## Multi-Currency FX Snapshot

Every `Transaction` and `Ledger` row carries an FX snapshot:
`exchange_rate` (default `1.0`), `exchange_rate_date`, and `base_amount`
(in the entity's functional currency). Single-currency entities see no
behavior change — `exchange_rate=1.0` makes `base_amount == amount`.
Multi-currency entities use `base_amount` for consolidated reporting.

### 🛑 Aggregation rule for ALL future development

Any new SQL aggregation, report, dashboard, or analytics query that sums/averages
monetary fields on `Transaction` or `Ledger` **must** coalesce to the base mirror.
Plain references to `amount` will silently mix currencies for any entity that ever
has a foreign-currency transaction.

```python
# SQLAlchemy:
from sqlalchemy import func
func.sum(func.coalesce(Ledger.base_amount, Ledger.amount))
func.sum(func.coalesce(Transaction.base_amount, Transaction.main_account_amount))

# Raw SQL:
SELECT SUM(COALESCE(base_amount, amount)) FROM ledger WHERE entity_id = :eid;
SELECT SUM(COALESCE(base_amount, main_account_amount)) FROM transaction
  WHERE entity_id = :eid AND transaction_type = 'CLIENT_INVOICE';
```

The COALESCE handles two cases uniformly: legacy rows (pre-multi-currency
migration, `base_amount` is NULL) fall through to the native field; current
rows in the entity's functional currency have `base_amount = amount` after the
migration's idempotent backfill.

**v1 boundary (deferred to v1.1):** today `Account.closing_balance`
(`src/accounting/models/account.py`) sums `Ledger.amount` filtered by
`currency_id = self.currency_id` — naturally correct per-account but does not
consolidate across mixed-currency accounts. Switching to
`func.sum(func.coalesce(Ledger.base_amount, Ledger.amount))` (and dropping the
currency_id filter) gives byte-identical results for single-currency entities and
correct consolidation for multi-currency. Apply this swap to `IncomeStatement`,
`BalanceSheet`, and `AgingSchedule` reports in the same pass when adopting v1.1.

**CRM-side aggregation rule** (Opportunity / Order / Invoice on MongoDB) uses the
`$ifNull` Mongo equivalent — see the Ambivo CRM API spec.

### ⚠️ FX rate convention — direct quote (Wise-style)

`Transaction.exchange_rate` follows the same convention as the CRM side:

> **Rate is "units of TO per 1 unit of FROM."**
> Direction: `from = transaction.currency_id` (transaction currency),
> `to = entity.currency_id` (functional currency).
> Math: `base_amount = main_account_amount × exchange_rate`.

This matches Wise, ECB, OpenExchangeRates, Fixer, Currencylayer, and most major FX
APIs. Concrete: for a EUR Bill on a USD entity when 1 EUR ≈ 1.18 USD, the
`transaction.exchange_rate` is stored as `1.18` and `transaction.base_amount =
main_account_amount × 1.18`.

**This is the OPPOSITE of NetSuite's classic indirect-quote convention** (where rate
is "units of FROM per 1 unit of TO" and you'd divide). If a future engineer ever
hooks up an FX provider or imports historical rates that use NetSuite's convention,
they **MUST invert the rate before persisting** to `transaction.exchange_rate` —
otherwise a 1000 EUR Bill on a USD entity would be saved as `base_amount = 1000 /
1.18 ≈ 847` USD (half the right answer; the error compounds as `rate²` on reports).

Sync from Core API (CRM Invoice → Books Transaction via `accounting_sync_webhook`)
already passes the rate through unchanged — both systems use the same convention.

## Frontend Business Flows

### 1. Authentication & Entity Setup
1. `POST /auth/login` → receive JWT + `tenant_dict` (includes `invoicing_system`)
2. If MFA required: `POST /auth/mfa/verify` with challenge code
3. `GET /auth/entities` → list available entities for tenant
4. If no entities: redirect to setup → `POST /entities/setup` (creates entity + default Chart of Accounts)
5. `POST /auth/set-entity` → set active entity context for the session

### 2. Invoice Lifecycle (Invoices Page)
1. **Create**: `POST /invoices/core-invoices` (can save as draft or post immediately)
   - **Edit**: `PATCH /invoices/core-invoices/{id}` → lines, customer and date while unposted; description, due date and terms at any time
2. **Finalize/Post**: `POST /invoices/core-invoices/{id}/finalize` → moves draft→open, creates GL entry
3. **Send via Stripe**: `POST /stripe-invoices/{id}/send` → emails customer with hosted payment URL
4. **Record Payment**: `POST /invoices/core-invoices/{id}/payment` → updates stage to partial/paid
5. **Void**: `POST /invoices/core-invoices/{id}/void` → creates reversing GL entry
- **QuickBooks guard**: If `invoicing_system="quickbooks"`, only viewing is allowed (403 on CUD)

### 3. Bill Lifecycle (Bills Page)
1. **Create**: `POST /bills` → creates bill in Core API (MongoDB)
2. **Edit**: `PUT /bills/{id}`
3. **Record Payment**: `POST /bills/{id}/payment` → records payment + creates GL entry
4. **Pay via Wise**: Multi-step international wire flow:
   - `GET /wise-payments/recipients` → find/create recipient
   - `POST /wise-payments/quote` → get exchange rate + fees
   - `POST /wise-payments/pay` → execute payment with Stripe charge + Wise transfer
5. **Void**: `POST /bills/{id}/void` → creates reversing GL entry
6. **Void Payment**: `POST /bills/{id}/payments/{payment_id}/void`

### 4. Bank Connection Linking (Bank Accounts Page)
1. **Connect Bank**: `POST /bank-connections/link-session` → get `client_secret` + `publishable_key`
2. Frontend calls `stripe.collectFinancialConnectionsAccounts({ clientSecret })` → Stripe modal
3. **Sync**: `POST /bank-connections/sync` → creates BankAccountMapping rows in PostgreSQL
4. **Link to GL Account**: `POST /bank-connections/{fca_xxx}/link-account` → associates FC account with Books BANK account
5. **Attach Payment Method**: `POST /bank-connections/{fca_xxx}/attach-payment-method` → enables ACH payments
6. **Sync Transactions**: `POST /bank-connections/{fca_xxx}/sync-transactions` → pulls bank txns into PostgreSQL

### 5. Bank Reconciliation (Bank Transactions Page)
1. **Auto-match**: `POST /bank-transactions/auto-match` → engine matches by amount+date
2. **Manual match**: `POST /bank-transactions/{id}/match` with `books_transaction_id`
3. **Match to Invoice**: `GET .../invoice-suggestions` → `POST .../match-invoice` (records payment too)
4. **Match to Bill**: `GET .../bill-suggestions` → `POST .../match-bill` (records payment too)
5. **Create Expense**: `POST .../create-expense` → creates accounting entry from bank txn
6. **Exclude/Include**: `POST .../exclude` or `POST .../include`

### 6. Financial Reports (Reports Page)
- `GET /reports/trial-balance?as_of_date=YYYY-MM-DD`
- `GET /reports/income-statement?start_date=...&end_date=...`
- `GET /reports/balance-sheet?as_of_date=YYYY-MM-DD`
- `GET /reports/cashflow-statement?start_date=...&end_date=...`
- `GET /reports/aging/receivables` and `GET /reports/aging/payables`
- PDF export is client-side only (html2pdf.js)

### 7. Data Import (Import Pages)
1. **Chart of Accounts**: Upload CSV → `POST /imports/chart-of-accounts/validate` → `POST /imports/chart-of-accounts`
2. **Trial Balance**: Upload CSV → `POST /imports/trial-balance/validate` → `POST /imports/trial-balance`
3. **Combined**: `POST /imports/combined` (atomic: both or neither)
4. **Bank Transactions CSV**: `POST /manual-bank-accounts/{id}/transactions/validate` → `POST .../import`

### 8. Manual Bank Accounts (Bank Accounts Page)
1. **Create**: `POST /manual-bank-accounts` → creates manual account + BankAccountMapping
2. **Import CSV**: navigate to `/manual-bank-accounts/{id}/import` → validate + import
3. **Undo Import**: `DELETE /manual-bank-accounts/{id}/import-batches/{batch_id}`

## Breaking changes — GET /api/v1/bank-transactions

This endpoint now implements the uniform list contract:

- **Unknown query params are rejected with 422**, not ignored. Previously an
  unsupported or misspelled param was silently dropped and the endpoint returned the
  UNFILTERED set with HTTP 200 — a wrong answer that looked like a right one.
- **`page` and `search` are deprecated aliases** for `page_num` and `search_text`.
  Both are still accepted; the contract name wins if both are sent.
- `total` is nullable (`get_count=false` → `total: null`, meaning *not counted*).
  Use `has_more`, which is derived from a limit+1 probe and is exact.

- access_token: Microsoft OAuth access token (required)
- device_id: Device identifier (optional)
- os: Operating system (optional)

Login with Apple.

Proxies to core API: POST /user/login_with_apple

Request body (JSON):
- apple_id: Apple ID (required)
- apple_meta: Apple metadata (optional)

For verification:
- userid: User ID (required)
- provider_challenge_id: Challenge ID (required)
- challenge_code: MFA code (required)

For resend:

- userid: User ID (required)
- provider_challenge_id: Challenge ID (required)

Send or verify a phone OTP code.

Proxies to core API: POST /admin/sms/verifications

including result:3 (tenant selection required) and result:2 (error).

Request body (JSON):
- action: "send_verification_code" or "verify_code"
- phone_number: Phone number in E.164 format
- code: 5-digit OTP code (verify_code only)
- tenant_id: Tenant ID for multi-tenant disambiguation (optional)
- device_id: Device identifier (optional)
- os: Operating system (optional)

Used when a third-party system (OAuth callback, email confirmation, etc.)

calls this endpoint to resolve it into a full login session.

Request body (JSON):
- token: JWT token or temporary exchange token
- device_id: Device identifier (optional)

get.description:
Which entity this session's writes will land in.

⭐⭐ REPORTS THE EFFECTIVE ENTITY, NOT ONLY AN EXPLICIT CHOICE. This used to
return null whenever Redis held no selection — while `get_current_entity_id`
(deps.py) went right ahead and resolved the tenant's lowest-id entity for
every write. So the endpoint whose entire job is naming the current entity
disagreed with the entity actually used, and said "none" at precisely the
moment a caller most needed an answer.

That is not a cosmetic gap. A phone posting expenses cannot show the person
which company's books they are writing to, and a wrong entity that nobody
can see is two companies' books quietly merged, discovered at year-end.

`is_default` distinguishes the two cases, because they need different words:
a chosen entity is a fact, a defaulted one is an assumption worth flagging.

⚠ READ-ONLY. `get_current_entity_id` writes its resolution back to Redis;
this must not, or merely LOOKING at the context would pin it — and the
Redis key includes `client_connection_id`, which is minted fresh on every
login, so a pin made here would silently expire at the next sign-in anyway.

List all entities (companies) for the current tenant.

Returns only entities that belong to the authenticated user's tenant.

Accepts the uniform list contract (`match_filter_dict` / `sort_dict` /
`page_num` / `page_size` / `search_text` / `get_count`; see
`docs/list_contract.md`). Tenant scope is applied in the service from the
caller's token and is ANDed with the filter -- nothing on the wire can widen
it. Unknown query params are REJECTED (422) rather than ignored.

This now pages in SQL instead of slicing the whole tenant's entity list in
Python. The row SET is unchanged, soft-deleted entities included, because
quietly changing which rows a list returns is a worse surprise than the
inconsistency; `deleted_at` is filterable so a caller can ask for live ones.

Entity options for a dropdown or a reference column.

**Mode A — browse/search** (`?search_text=&page_num=&page_size=`) returns
`PicklistResponse`: `{items:[{id,name}], total, page, page_size, has_more}`.

**Mode B — resolve** (`?ids=1,2,3`) returns `PicklistResolveResponse`:
`{items:[{id,name}], missing:[...]}` and no paging keys, which are meaningless
for an id set. An id that does not resolve is reported in `missing`, never a
404 — one deleted reference must not blank a whole grid.

`response_model` is left unset on purpose: a `Union` of the two shapes would
let pydantic validate a mode-A response against the mode-B model (its extra
keys are simply dropped and `missing` defaults to `[]`), silently deleting the
paging keys. Returning the model instance keeps each mode's shape exact.

Set up the first entity (company) for a new tenant.

This endpoint is specifically for users who have no entities yet.
It creates the entity along with its default currency and optionally
sets up a chart of accounts based on the selected preset.

Unlike the regular create endpoint, this does not require an existing entity context.

Account presets:
- 'basic': Essential accounts only (7 accounts)
- 'standard': Common business accounts (27 accounts)
- 'full': Comprehensive chart of accounts (80+ accounts)

This is idempotent — if books is already enabled, returns the current state.

get.description:
Get accounts picklist for dropdown selection. Two modes on one endpoint.

**Mode A — browse/search** (`?search_text=&page_num=&page_size=`): a
paginated, searchable list. Used by Core API and by every screen that lets a
user pick a GL Account — product income/expense/asset accounts, product tax
codes, customer/vendor defaults, invoice A/R and deposit accounts.

**Mode B — resolve** (`?ids=1,2,3`): the labels for a known id set, so a grid
with N account reference cells costs ONE request instead of N `getOne()`
calls. A missing id is an OMISSION reported in `missing`, never a 404 — one
deleted reference must not blank a whole grid.

`response_model` is deliberately unset: the two modes return different
shapes, and a Union response model would let pydantic coerce a mode-A body
into the mode-B shape (every field of which has a default) and silently drop
the paging keys.

post.description:
"Post to books": post the invoice's CLIENT_INVOICE entry and move the Core
invoice from `draft` to `open`.

The entry is committed before Core's stage moves, so the notice Core sends
for the stage change finds it and does nothing. Core's stage is read back to
confirm the move, then `books_accounting_status` and `books_transaction_id`
are stamped on the Core invoice.

- An invoice already `open` with an entry: no-op.
- An invoice `open` without an entry: the entry is created; the stage stays.
- The entry cannot be posted: 409, and nothing changes.
- Core keeps the invoice in `draft`: the entry is reversed, 502.
- Core cannot be read back: the entry stays posted, 502. Calling again
  finishes the move.
- The invoice is linked to Stripe (`stripe_invoice_id`): 409, before
  anything is posted. Core cannot move its stage; Stripe opens it and Books
  posts it then. A Stripe tenant's manual invoice (no Stripe link) posts.
- The invoice is an opening balance (`books_accounting_status` is
  `not_required`, from Core's import): 409, and nothing is posted. The
  opening trial balance already holds it.

get.description:
Generate accounts receivable aging schedule.

Shows outstanding client invoices grouped by age buckets:
- Current (0-30 days)
- 31-60 days
- 61-90 days
- Over 90 days

Ages the invoices Core still reports as outstanding — stage `open`.

⚠ A FULLY PAID INVOICE CAN STILL BE STAGE `open`. Core now advances the stage
when a payment clears the balance, but that fix is forward-only — every invoice
settled before it stays `open` for good, and on the tenant this was built
against that is 3,972 of 4,365.

So the stage cannot decide what is outstanding, and the reported BALANCE is
what keeps a settled invoice out of this report: a mirrored document has no
assignments here, so `amount - cleared` would return the full invoice forever.
Aged at the balance, a paid invoice reports 0 and drops out.

An invoice with no accounting entry is aged from the Core document itself, so
the figure is right on the first load. Nothing is posted during this GET.

Excludes drafts, cancelled and voided invoices and anything written off as
uncollectible.

Bank-account options for a dropdown or a reference column.

Manual accounts are referenced by id from other screens — the bank-transaction
register filters on `bank_account_mapping_id` and the check dialog draws on
one — so both modes matter here.

**Mode A — browse/search** (`?search_text=&page_num=&page_size=`) returns
`PicklistResponse`: `{items:[{id,name}], total, page, page_size, has_more}`.

**Mode B — resolve** (`?ids=1,2,3`) returns `PicklistResolveResponse`:
`{items:[{id,name}], missing:[...]}` and no paging keys. An id that does not
resolve is reported in `missing`, never a 404 — one deleted reference must not
blank a whole grid.

`response_model` is left unset on purpose: a `Union` of the two shapes would
let pydantic validate a mode-A response against the mode-B model (its extra
keys are dropped and `missing` defaults to `[]`), silently deleting the paging
keys. Returning the model instance keeps each mode's shape exact.

Accepts the uniform list contract (`match_filter_dict` / `sort_dict` /
`page_num` / `page_size` / `search_text`; see `docs/list_contract.md`). Field
names are validated against `registries/check_registry.py` before anything
leaves Books — an undeclared key is a 400 naming it, never a filter Core
quietly ignores while returning the unfiltered set.

Macros (`datetime(...)`, `{{token}}`, `expr(...)`) are resolved to concrete
values here. That is what makes forwarding safe: a resolved value is
idempotent under Core's own interpolation pass, whereas a token's fate varies
per endpoint.

Two honest limits worth knowing:

* **Scope is Core's, and it is by TENANT.** Core stamps `tenant_id` onto the
  query after copying the caller's keys, so no caller-supplied scope key is
  honoured. `micr_checks` has no entity dimension at all, so `entity_id` here
  only selects which Books bank names are matched for display — checks from
  another entity in the same tenant are still listed. Pre-existing.
* **`get_count` is accepted and costs nothing either way.** Core returns its
  count in the same response as the rows, so there is no second query to skip
  — and passing Core's own `get_count` would make it return the count INSTEAD
  of the rows. `total` therefore stays populated regardless.

SendCoreInvoiceResponse.title: SendCoreInvoiceResponse
SendCoreInvoiceResponse.description:
The outcome of a send.

⭐ IT REPORTS `queued`, NOT `delivered`. Core hands the mail to an event queue
and a periodic callback does the work later, so no synchronous response can
know whether it arrived — every real failure (no usable recipient, a connected
mailbox whose OAuth has lapsed, no transport) happens on that later pass and
only logs. An earlier version of this model claimed `delivered` and was
hard-coded true by construction, which is worse than saying nothing.

⭐ `queued: false` still arrives with a 200 and a real `pdf_url`. The document
rendered; raising would throw away a link the caller can use. Read `queued`,
not the status code.

WiseTransferStatus.title: WiseTransferStatus
WiseTransferStatus.description:
The Wise transfer lifecycle, as stored.

Declared here rather than imported because these are Wise's own status
strings mirrored onto the document -- Books has no enum for them, and a
``SELECT`` without an ``enum_cls`` would validate nothing while implying it
does.

⚠ THE SOURCE OF TRUTH IS ``WISE_TRANSFER_STATUSES`` in ambivo-nx
(``libs/books/data/src/lib/objects/wise-transfer.object.ts``), which was
confirmed against real data and against the React screen that shipped before
it. It is NOT the lifecycle sketch in ``WiseTransfer``'s docstring
(``ambivo_api/src/omnilonely/data/wise.py:104-106``).

I built this list from that docstring first and it was wrong in both
directions: it omitted ``funds_refunded`` / ``charged_back`` / ``failed``, so
the register's "Failed or bounced" card -- which asks for all four at once --
came back 400 and rendered no number at all; and it added ``completed``,
which appears in the sketch but which the client does not use.

``completed`` is kept because refusing a status that does occur breaks a
card, while accepting one that never occurs only ever matches nothing. The
asymmetry is the whole reason to err wide here.

``authorization_hold`` is Ambivo's, not Wise's: it is the pre-send hold the
cancel path special-cases (``wise_service.cancel_transfer``), and the one
state where the money has NOT moved and the transfer can still be cancelled.

AccountPicklistResponse.description:
Response for account picklist (mode A -- browse/search).

The contract's `PicklistResponse` carries only `{id, name}`. This route
predates it and its shipped client (`account-picklist.api.ts`) reads
`account_code` / `account_type` / `fully_qualified_name`, so the item shape
stays as it is; the paging keys below are ADDED, not swapped in.

`total_count` keeps its original meaning -- the number of items in THIS
response -- because that is what existing callers already read. The real
matching count is `total`, which is null when the caller passed
`get_count=false`. Two fields rather than one repurposed field: silently
changing what `total_count` counts is exactly the kind of confident wrong
number this contract exists to remove.
